3) Let, length of each side of $ABCD$ is $10 \text{ cm}$ and the diagonals intersect each other at the point $O$.

We know, diagonals of rhombus bisect each other at right angle.

$\therefore OA = OC, OB = OD$

In the right-angled triangle $\triangle AOB$, hypotenuse $AB = 10$

Here, $AB^2 = 10^2 = 100 = 36 + 64$

$= 6^2 + 8^2 = OB^2 + OA^2$ [according to the figure]

$\therefore OB = 6, OA = 8$

$\therefore$ diagonal $AC = 2 \times 8 = 16 \text{ cm}$ and diagonal $BD = 2 \times 6 = 12 \text{ cm}$

$\therefore$ area of the rhombus $ABCD = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BD = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 12 = 96 \text{ square cm}$
